title: Wipro Says PERM Suspension Won't Materially Hurt Business, Cites 80% Local US Hiring
excerpt: The BSE filing stresses that PERM is a green-card pathway distinct from H-1B — but workers relying on a pending PERM for H-1B extensions remain exposed.
body:
• Wipro told the BSE on Tuesday that the US Department of Labor's suspension of new PERM applications for certain companies is unlikely to have a material business impact on it.
  • More than 80 percent of Wipro's US workforce is locally hired — the result of a deliberate localisation strategy the company has pursued for years.
  • PERM is one specific pathway to permanent residency and is separate from the H-1B visa programme, Wipro noted.
  • For Indian tech workers: Kotak says the workers most exposed are those relying on a pending PERM to extend H-1B status beyond six years; approved I-140 holders face limited direct impact.

Wipro has become the latest Indian IT major to tell investors that Washington's freeze on green-card labour certifications will not materially hurt its business, citing a US workforce that is now more than 80 percent locally hired.

In a filing with the BSE on Tuesday, reported by The Hindu BusinessLine and Mint, the company said the Department of Labor's suspension of new applications under the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme "relates to a specific pathway to permanent residency and is distinct from broader skilled talent mobility programmes such as the H-1B visa." Wipro said it would continue to invest in local talent, comply with US laws and ensure business continuity for clients.

The suspension

The Labor Department announced last week that it was suspending new PERM applications — and, per reports, pausing processing of pending ones — for a group of companies that includes TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, Wipro, Cognizant and Capgemini, alongside Microsoft and Adobe. PERM is the labour certification an employer must obtain before sponsoring a worker for an employment-based green card; it is a residency step, not a work visa. The administration has accused the named companies of displacing US workers, a charge the industry disputes. The department has not said how long the suspension will last.

https://x.com/businessline/status/2110035876487000409

Why the companies are calm

Wipro's statement follows the same line Infosys took last week. A Kotak Institutional Equities note on October 12 reached the same conclusion from the outside: visa-dependent employees are a small and shrinking share of Indian IT firms' US workforces, employees with pending PERM applications are a smaller subset still, and delivery and earnings should see no meaningful impact. Kotak expects firms to lean further into local hiring, use subcontractors for immediate needs at some near-term cost, and shift more work offshore to offset it.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=V3SAYBJxGTg

"Over the years, Wipro has pursued a deliberate localisation strategy in the US, with more than 80% of our workforce in the country locally hired."

— Wipro, in its BSE filing

What it means if you work in the US on a visa

The business impact and the personal impact are different questions. Your H-1B status is not revoked by a PERM suspension, and Kotak notes that workers with an approved I-140 petition face limited direct exposure. The exposed group is narrower and specific: employees counting on a PERM filing — or the I-140 that follows it — to extend H-1B status beyond the standard six-year limit. For them, a paused pipeline creates a timing problem that only their employer's immigration counsel can map against their individual dates. Anyone in that position should ask for that mapping now rather than assume the suspension is a non-event.

What's next

The open variables are duration and scope: how long the suspension runs, whether pending applications resume processing, and whether the Labor Department extends the list of companies. Until the department clarifies, the filings from Wipro and Infosys amount to the industry position — operations insulated by local hiring, individual green-card timelines not.
